hints.title: Greedy Highest Value Priority
hints.text: To maximize the subset sum, always prefer items with larger values. Pair each value with its label and sort in descending order of value.

hints.title: Label Quota Tracking
hints.text: Keep track of how many items with each label have been selected using a frequency counter. Skip any item whose label has already reached useLimit.

hints.title: Stop at Wanted Count
hints.text: Iterate through the sorted pairs. Whenever an item is accepted, increment the label count and add its value to total sum. Terminate once numWanted items are chosen.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def largestValsFromLabels(self, values: list[int], labels: list[int], numWanted: int, useLimit: int) -> int:
        items = sorted(zip(values, labels), key=lambda x: -x[0])
        label_counts = defaultdict(int)
        total = 0
        taken = 0
        for v, l in items:
            if label_counts[l] < useLimit:
                total += v
                label_counts[l] += 1
                taken += 1
                if taken == numWanted:
                    break
        return total
```

variables: N: number of items in values array
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Knapsack-like dynamic programming is unnecessary when weights are identical (1 item each).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting pairs and greedily picking valid items runs in O(N log N) time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that identical item weights enable greedy selection by descending value with label quota.
complexity.notes: Stops early once numWanted items are accumulated.
